A store-side staleness measurement alone cannot separate them -- staleness is the observation both hypotheses predict -- so the trigger read had to come first and did.
preRegistered: (a) is CORRECT if and only if a cron / Cloud Run job schedule / queue consumer is found that runs factory-bastrop-publish (or any bake CLI) on a cadence. Predicted by the row's own framing ('do not assume the cheap one'), so (a) was the expectation to beat, not the default.
(b) is CORRECT if factory-bastrop-publish has no scheduling resource and no code path in the cell writers enqueues a parcel.
Mixed is possible: (b) with a partial (a) if some other actor (a lane, a manual step, a different scheduled job) re-bakes whole counties.
